questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write a best-selling book
Why bookshops are closing in the UK
The history of the Great Depression
Why the self-help industry is so successful
questions.why: Rob says the topic is self-help and the self-help industry, and they look at why it does so well.

questions.q: What does the $10bn US self-help industry include, according to Rob?
options: Only books and magazines sold in bookshops
Gym memberships, diet plans and coaching apps
Doctors, hospitals and medicine for stress
University courses in psychology and business
questions.why: Rob says it includes gym memberships, diet plans and life coaching apps.

questions.q: According to bookshop manager Emma Marshall, what is the trend at the moment?
options: Tidying up and getting rid of things
Colouring-in books for adults
Books about getting rich quickly
Books about travel and adventure
questions.why: She says 'at the moment we're in the tidying up, getting rid of things trend'.

questions.q: What does Neil say about books on tidying up?
options: He has already read several and found them useful
He thinks they are a waste of money and paper
He'd more likely buy the book than actually tidy
He tidies every day without any help from books
questions.why: Neil jokes, 'I'd be more likely to buy a book about it than actually tidy up!'

questions.q: What is happening to the colouring-in trend?
options: It is growing fast
It is only popular with children
It is becoming less popular
It has just started
questions.why: Emma says colouring-in is 'dwindling now', and Neil says they're selling fewer of these books.

questions.q: What does psychologist Dr Jennifer Wild think is a big reason for the industry's success?
options: The internet, where we're used to searching for solutions
Cheaper books sold in supermarkets and at stations
Advice from doctors who recommend self-help books
Television programmes about people changing their lives
questions.why: She believes the internet is a big factor, as we're used to searching for solutions online.

questions.q: What does Caroline Beaton say about millennials?
options: They are lazy and never buy any self-help products
They're very self-critical and spend twice as much as Gen X
They prefer self-help books written in the 1930s
They spend much less on self-help than older people
questions.why: She says millennials are highly self-critical and spend twice as much as Generation Xers.

questions.q: Why does the self-help industry do well even in a recession?
options: Self-help books become much cheaper when money is short
Governments pay for self-help courses for unemployed people
People have more free time to read when they lose their jobs
People may turn to self-help more to improve their situation
questions.why: Rob says when the economy does badly, people may be even more likely to reach for self-help.
